PL-44.body: The ring is drawn here by its source page’s own code (the record atlas on the Mindgut launch page), at the plate’s resolution. The finish and its field or light are the page’s own controls; spike reach, the inner cut and the engraved line pitch are the numbers its drawing is built from, read live.
PL-44.colorHint: These are the inks the ring’s own drawing calls use: the crossing dots, the address in the center, its caption and the contour. The thermal and engraved fills are laid pixel by pixel and keep their own colors.

ctl.label: Finish
ctl.note: The page’s own three renderings of the ring: engraved line, numbered cells, or a thermal field.

ctl.label: Spike reach
ctl.note: How far each crossing pushes the contour out: radius = 1 + reach × its distance from the baseline. The page’s own is 4.2; at 1 the ring is nearly round. Read on a log track, so equal travel gives an equal change in the spikes.

ctl.label: Inner cut
ctl.note: The inner contour, as a share of each crossing’s radius: it follows the spikes, so this sets how wide the cut band is. The page’s own is 64%; below 60% the band reaches the address, above 68% the numbered finish loses its cells at the spike tips.

ctl.label: Field variation
ctl.note: The page’s field-variation slider for the thermal field: stirs the color inside the cut contour; the held coordinates stay put.

ctl.label: Light direction
ctl.note: The page’s own light for the numbered finish: the depth × light ramp the digits 1–9 are read from.

ctl.label: Line pitch
ctl.note: Spacing of the engraved lines, in the page’s pixels on its 420 px ring. The page’s own is 3.6.

PL-14.body: The ring is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Lab 2 of the Mindgut Exhibition). Each dial is one of that lab’s own controls: tilt, strands, radial gain, the layer it is drawn in, and the recall chords.

ctl.label: Tilt
ctl.note: The lab’s tilt: 0 looks down the axis of the record; a few degrees show its turns stacking behind one another. Past 5° the turns close into a coil and the ring is lost.

ctl.label: Strands
ctl.note: How many strands of the record are drawn, each seeded by one line: 42 make a turn, 126 three, 210 five.

ctl.label: Radial gain
ctl.note: How far each strand reaches from the ring for its weight.

ctl.label: Layer
ctl.note: Which of the lab’s four layers draws the ring: dots, path, contours or glow.

ctl.label: Recall chords
ctl.note: The chords from the newest strand back to the strands it recalls.

PL-14.colorHint: Source is the lab’s own night rendering: the record in light, glowing on its void. Paper is the lab’s own print rendering of the same record: darker inks multiplied on paper, chords and seed ring in ink.

PL-126.body: The figure is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Crystal optics territory, plate 01). Each dial is one of the page’s own controls: the defect, the polarizer angle, the retardance and the 530 nm plate.

ctl.label: Defect
ctl.note: The defect in the crystal: a Maltese cross (s = +1, four brushes), two half-defects (s = ±½, two brushes each), or a schlieren field.

ctl.label: Polarizer angle
ctl.note: Turns the crossed polarizers; the brushes turn with them.

ctl.label: Retardance
ctl.note: Γ = d·Δn where the crystal is thickest (it falls to 130 nm at its thinnest). More retardance climbs more Michel-Lévy orders: gray, yellow, first-order red, teal.

ctl.label: 530 nm plate
ctl.note: The first-order red plate (530 nm) laid in at 45°: retardance adds where the crystal’s slow axis runs with the plate and subtracts across it, so the colors split blue and yellow by the sign of the defect, and thin, isotropic ground shows its magenta.

PL-148.body: The drawing is made here by its source page’s own code (reference 010, built from the concept end), full bleed as filed. Each switch is one of the page’s own: the grammar measured or plain, and each of its passes on or off. The keyline weight is the grammar’s measured key, read live.

ctl.label: Grammar
ctl.note: Measured draws with the whole grammar; Plain keeps only the flat fills, for comparison. While Plain, the pass switches rest.

ctl.label: Fills
ctl.note: The flat inks of every shape: green cast, cream paper, brown wood. Off leaves each shape in plain paper.

ctl.label: Stacks
ctl.note: The envelope stack’s edge rules at the measured 4 px pitch, alternating a full and a thin line.

ctl.label: Marks
ctl.note: The drawn details: dial ticks and needle, the address hand, stamp and postmark, the name-plate rules, the wood grain.

ctl.label: Key
ctl.note: The measured 1 px keyline around every shape; off, the fills meet edge to edge.

ctl.label: Keyline weight
ctl.note: Width of the key in the drawing’s reference pixels (1000 across). The measured key is 1 px; the thin rules of the stacks and marks stay half of it.

ctl.label: Texture
ctl.note: Per-ink grain at each ink’s measured strength, fine and unrepeated; the keylines stay clean.

PL-57.body: The stack is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Mindgut landing page V01). The step is the page’s own control; layer gap, axis angle, the unlit plates and the keyline are the numbers its drawing is built from, read live, with the drawing refit to its frame.

ctl.label: Step
ctl.note: The page’s four steps through the stack: say, count, keep, reach back. Each lights its plate and its leader.

ctl.label: Layer gap
ctl.note: How far the plates are drawn apart, as a share of a plate’s length. The page’s own is 72.5% (5.8 of 8 units); below 66% the tallest count block reaches the plate above. The drawing is refit to its frame.

ctl.label: Axis angle
ctl.note: The angle the plates’ edges make with the horizontal, set by how high the eye sits: 30° is isometric. Lower flattens the plates; higher opens them up toward a plan, up to where the blocks would reach the plate above.

ctl.label: Unlit plates
ctl.note: How strongly the plates off the current step show. The page’s own is 50%; at 100% every plate is lit alike and the step is marked only by its lime edge.

ctl.label: Keyline
ctl.note: Weight of the drawing’s object lines (plates, blocks, ticks, recall rings) in the page’s pixels; the plate edges and the lit edge keep their proportion. Leaders and the dimension stay hairline.

PL-55.body: The field is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Mindgut Worlds V2), with the type the page sets over it. Each dial is one of the page’s own controls: the world and Mir’s presence state.

ctl.label: World
ctl.note: The page’s three worlds: signal as sculpture, memory, or words under pressure.

ctl.sel: main:nth-child(2) > section:nth-child(5) > div:nth-child(1) > div:nth-child(1) > div:nth-child(4) > button
ctl.label: Presence
ctl.note: Mir’s presence on the page: listening, reaching, or at rest.
